title: Emergency model hotpatch and rollback procedure
author: Aisha Malik
body:
Overview:
This runbook defines a safe, auditable process for performing emergency hotpatches and full rollbacks of model deployments in production. The goal is to restore SLO compliance and prevent client-impacting behavioral regressions while preserving traceability for post-incident review. This document is intended for SRE and Serving Runtime on-call engineers, Product Engineers owning model behavior, and Platform Engineers coordinating infrastructure changes.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to model variants serving text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted and Dedicated environments. Does NOT cover private on-prem control-plane changes (those follow the Private Ops handbook).
- Describes two corrective actions: (A) hotpatch (code/config/feature gate change that preserves model binary), (B) rollback (reverting to a previous pinned model version).
- Includes decision criteria, preconditions, step-by-step procedures, verification checks, and communication templates.

Key principles:
- Minimum blast radius: prefer targeted hotpatches that scope to affected tenants or routes before global changes.
- SLO-first: actions triggered when SLO deviation or error-budget burn meets thresholds defined in the Decision Criteria section.
- Observable and reversible: all changes must be automated through the deployment pipeline and provide an automated rollback path.
- Post-action evidence: collect telemetry and artifact snapshots for incident review.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Oncall SRE (owner): owns execution, live coordination, and final go/no-go on rollbacks/hotpatches.
- Serving Runtime Engineer (runtime): implements hotpatch (binary-safe config changes, KV cache eviction), monitors resource impact, and adjusts autoscaling as needed.
- Model Owner/Product Engineer (product): provides behavioral criteria (regression test set, golden prompts) and approves rollbacks that could impact model correctness.
- Release Engineer (release): runs the CI/CD pipeline, verifies artifacts, and ensures deployment manifests are signed.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates cross-team comms, customer-facing messaging, and retro assignment.

Decision criteria (when to hotpatch vs rollback):
1) Triage severity and SLO impact:
   - If P99 latency or 95th percentile error rate crosses service SLO by >3x and persists for >5 minutes -> action required.
   - If error budget projected to be exhausted within the hour -> action required.
2) Behavioral regression vs infra fault:
   - Behavioral (e.g., hallucination spike, safety filter failures): prefer rollback to last known-good model variant if hotspot affects >10% of requests or cannot be mitigated by a config change.
   - Infra (OOMs, CUDA driver regressions, kernel-level stalls): prefer hotpatch (runtime config change, memory throttling) and capacity adjustments.
3) Availability of canary/blue-green targets:
   - If a verified canary model exists with <1% divergence on regression set, prefer canary promote instead of rollback.
4) Customer blast radius:
   - If only VIP tenants are affected, prefer tenant-scoped hotpatch or targeted routing.

Preconditions and safety checks (must pass before making changes):
- SLO and error-budget dashboards live and accessible. Take a screenshot of current state.
- Deployment CI pipeline green for the artifact and integrity signature present.
- A test harness run: run the model regression test set (20–50 golden prompts) against target version; capture outputs.
- Capacity check: ensure headroom for rolling traffic (at least 25% spare GPU capacity per AZ or configured burst capacity).
- Approvals: Product Engineer and Serving Runtime must sign-off for rollback; SRE + Release Engineer for hotpatch. Document approval in the incident doc.

Emergency hotpatch procedure (short-lived, targeted fixes):
Purpose: apply a non-model-binary change that reduces client impact quickly (e.g., toggling safety filters, lowering max_tokens, disabling a problematic postprocessor, adjusting batching window).
Steps:
1) Prepare change in a hotpatch branch with a concise, reversible flag (featureflag: model_hotpatch_{incident_id}).
2) Run a dry-run locally against the canary cluster using the CI pipeline: `ci/deploy --dry-run --target canary --patch-flag=...`. Capture logs.
3) If dry-run passes, deploy to a single canary region and monitor these signals for 10 minutes:
   - Request success rate (1m/5m/15m)
   - Tail latency (p50/p95/p99) and queue length
   - Token throughput and GPU utilization
   - Golden prompt regressions (automated diff scoring)
4) If canary metrics are stable and regressions are within thresholds, orchestrate phased rollout: zone-by-zone, 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 30m windows. Pause and wait at each step for 5 full minutes.
5) If any metric worsens beyond kill-switch thresholds (see table below), immediately trigger automated rollback for that region and notify IC.
6) After full rollout, remove temporary flags within 72 hours or convert into permanent config with appropriate PR and review.

Automated kill-switch thresholds (examples):
- error_rate_increase > 200% vs baseline (5m)
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline
- customer-facing errors (5xx/invalid responses) > 0.5% of requests

Rollback procedure (reverting model version):
Purpose: when model behavior is the root cause or hotpatch is insufficient. Rollback is conservative because it changes served model artifacts.
Prerequisites: artifact of target model must be signed and present in artifact registry; previous version must be validated on regression harness.
Steps:
1) Confirm decision: Product Engineer and SRE agree that rollback is required. Document the rationale in the incident ticket (include golden prompt diffs).
2) Lock writes to model-routing config to prevent concurrent changes: `redwoodctl config lock model-routing --reason \"rollback-<incident_id>\"`
3) Promote previous model variant to canary with 1–2% traffic and run automated regression suite & telemetry for 10–15 minutes.
4) If canary is green, execute phased traffic shift using the traffic-controller tool: `redwoodctl traffic shift --model <prev_version> --policy phased --steps 10,30,60,100 --step-delay 1800s`
5) During each step, the SRE oncall must verify:SLO trends, error rates, customer telemetries/alerts, and resource utilization. If any step fails, abort and revert to pre-rollback state.
6) Once fully rolled back, mark the incident as "mitigated" and schedule a postmortem within 72 hours.

Post-action verification checklist:
- Confirm SLOs are trending back within expected bounds for 30–60 minutes.
- Verify no silent regressions by running full golden prompt suite (100+ prompts) and checking automatic diff metrics and human review samples for high-risk cases.
- Capture memory/GPU pressure metrics and ensure autoscaler did not thrash during the change.
- Export routing and model artifact manifests for evidence.

Operational tooling and commands (typical examples):
- `redwoodctl model list --env prod --format json` (list active variants)
- `redwoodctl traffic history --model <id> --window 1h` (audit last hour of routing decisions)
- `redwoodctl canary promote --model <id> --pct 2` (canary promote helper)
- CI pre-check example (YAML):
  - name: model-regression-check
    run: |
      python tools/regression_runner.py --model $MODEL_ID --prompts samples/golden_set.json --out /tmp/reg_out.json
- Example feature-flag toggle call (internal API):
  PATCH /flags/model-hotpatch/{flag}
  {\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"scope\": \"tenant:tenant-id-123\"\n  }

Telemetry and dashboards to consult (minimum):
- SLO dashboard: service/slo/model-inference (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, availability)
- Error budget burn: alerts for >30% burn in 1h or >70% projected in 6h
- Routing dashboard: model-routing/traffic-split (per-region, per-tenant)
- Regression scoring dashboard: evaluation/regression-diff (daily and live canary scoring)
- Resource dashboard: gpu-fleet/utilization, memory/oom-rate, scheduler-queue-length

Communication templates (IC -> stakeholders):
- Short status update (post-action):
  Subject: [INC <id>] Model mitigation executed — status: partial/complete
  Body: Action taken: rolled back model vX.Y or applied hotpatch flag model_hotpatch_<id>.
  Immediate impact: p99 latency down from Xms -> Yms; error rate reduced from A% -> B%.
  Next steps: monitoring for 60m, schedule postmortem, customer outreach if impacted.

- Customer-facing template (for affected tenants):
  Subject: Redwood Incident <id> — temporary mitigation applied
  Body: We identified a regression affecting inference quality/availability and applied an emergency mitigation to restore service. We are monitoring and will follow up with full postmortem.

Evidence collection for postmortem:
- Deploy manifests and `redwoodctl` audit logs for the time window (UTC timestamps).
- Golden prompt input/outputs before and after change (store in incident evidence bucket).
- SLO dashboard snapshots (PNG) and raw telemetry export (CSV) covering 2 hours before and 2 hours after action.
- Autoscaler and scheduler logs showing scaling events.

Testing and rehearsal guidance (reliability initiative tie-in):
- Run quarterly tabletop exercises focused on model rollback and hotpatch scenarios with sample failure injects (e.g., safety filter failure, embedding drift).
- Maintain a canary matrix: at least one verified canary per major model family with automated smoke tests run daily.
- Add a scheduled job that performs a dry-run of the rollback traffic-shift tool to validate automation and permissions.

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Owner: eng-sre (oncall runbook steward: Priya Kothari).
- Review cycle: annual or after any incident that exercises this runbook.
- Change process: all edits must be PR-reviewed by SRE + Serving Runtime and linked to a retro or incident ticket.

Appendix: thresholds table (copyable)
- severity_level | condition | action_required | approvals
- SEV2 | error_budget_burn_rate >= 30% in 1h | hotpatch/targeted rollback | SRE + runtime engineer
- SEV1 | error_budget_projection < 1h | immediate rollback & IC escalation | SRE + product + IC

Appendix: quick troubleshooting tips:
- If canary shows regressions but host metrics healthy: throttle to 0% and collect model outputs for human review.
- If OOMs spike post-rollback: temporarily reduce batching window and re-evaluate quantization profile for that variant.
- If autoscaler oscillates: increase cooldown to 10m and add capacity buffer of +15% for the rollback window.
